recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core FHIR follow-up is needed for FHIR-5198 unless a future Patient Administration decision changes the Appointment location modeling or search-parameter behavior.
issue_request: FHIR-5198 was a Published FHIR-core Patient Administration change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification for DSTU1, asking that Appointment support queries by location. The accepted resolution removed the standalone Appointment.location element, represented locations through participant.actor, added usage guidance, and included a search parameter specializing to that property.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by git commit 24ca87254f870290ca62f47e268355be7a08d5cd, which was titled "Tracker# 5198, 5199, 5299 Ballot Reconciliation updates(& QA clean-up)". That commit removed the old Appointment.location spreadsheet/example entry, added Location/HealthcareService to participant.actor, added Appointment location participation guidance, and added the Appointment location search parameter over Appointment.participant.actor.
additional_context: Appointment and AppointmentResponse are active resources in source/fhir.ini. Current Appointment source defines participant.actor as a Reference including HealthcareService and Location, current narrative says the location of the appointment is represented by a participant referencing Location or HealthcareService, and current search parameters include Appointment-location over Appointment.participant.actor.where(resolve() is Location). AppointmentResponse likewise permits Location on actor and has AppointmentResponse-location over AppointmentResponse.actor.where(resolve() is Location). Direct quoted Zulip and Confluence searches for FHIR-5198 plus Appointment location found no conflicting community record.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because the active current source already satisfies the FHIR-5198 resolution and no stale standalone Appointment.location element was found.

related_jiras.note: Co-applied in the same 2015 Appointment source commit, but it concerns v2 mappings rather than the location participant/search-parameter change and was not decided here.
